newsitem.title: USA: Imation Q2 revenues decline as expected.
newsitem.headline: Imation Q2 revenues decline as expected.

text.p: Imation Corp said Wednesday that second-quarter revenues declined 1.1 percent from a year ago, as expected, to $554.8 million.
Imation posted second-quarter net income of $4.4 million, versus a year-ago pro forma net loss of $37.8 million.

Adjusting for special charges of $66 million related to its July 1, 1996 spin-off from Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co, the company said it would have reported second quarter net income of $4.7 million in 1996.
The continued strength of the dollar reduced revenues by 4.4 percent and earnings per share by $0.06, said the imaging and information products and services company.
Pricing declines reduced revenues by 4.6 percent, in line with expectations, Imation said.
"The decline in second quarter revenues was also impacted by weaker than expected demand for certain lower-capacity data storage products," the company said.
Excluding special charges recognized in 1996, gross margin for the second quarter declined to 34.8 percent compared to 35.7 percent in the second quarter of last year.

"The strength of the dollar continues to have a negative impact on our results. In addition, a lower return from low-end tape storage products, combined with ramp-up costs of new hardware placements in DryView and tape libraries, hurt our overall gross margin," said chief executive Bill Monahan.

He added: "While this revenue mix contributed to disappointing results for the quarter, we expect that strong sales during the quarter of higher-capacity Travan 4 data cartridges, library tape cartridges and the growing base for future DryView film sales, translate into greater long-term benefit for Imation. At the same time we are working aggressively to improve our gross margin results."
